[b]Português[/b]
Embora o rFactor seja um jogo bem antigo, ele ainda tem seu valor nos dias de hoje, principalmente para quem joga em PC ou notebook fraco (que é a minha realidade por enquanto).

O menu é sim meio estranho e confuso no começo, mas depois que você se acostuma, fica simples de entender. Os gráficos são decentes para a época, e a física já é um pouco datada, porém ainda tem qualidade e potencial. O grande ponto forte do rFactor são os mods feitos pela comunidade. Existem várias temporadas completas que deixam o jogo muito mais vivo e diversificado. A maioria dos mods é de temporadas antigas da Fórmula 1, mas também é possível encontrar outras categorias. Além disso, os mods são bem simples de instalar.

Então, se você está procurando um jogo de corrida com carros, pistas e temporadas antigas, e tem um PC ou notebook mais fraco, esse jogo é pra você.

[b]Français[/b]
Même si rFactor est un jeu très ancien, il garde encore aujourd’hui une certaine valeur, surtout pour ceux qui jouent sur un PC ou un ordinateur portable peu puissant (ce qui est mon cas pour l’instant).

Le menu est effectivement un peu étrange et confus au début, mais une fois qu’on s’y habitue, il devient assez simple à comprendre. Les graphismes sont corrects pour l’époque, et la physique est un peu datée, mais elle reste de bonne qualité et avec encore du potentiel. Le gros point fort de rFactor, ce sont les mods créés par la communauté. Il existe de nombreuses saisons complètes qui rendent le jeu beaucoup plus vivant et varié. La majorité des mods concerne d’anciennes saisons de Formule 1, mais on peut aussi trouver d’autres catégories. En plus, les mods sont très faciles à installer.

Donc, si vous cherchez un jeu de course avec des voitures, des circuits et des saisons anciennes, et que vous avez un PC ou un laptop peu puissant, ce jeu est fait pour vous.

A trip down memory lane...
The year was 2008, I got a free 60 minute timed unlimited demo of Rfactor from some demo site. You could only play 60 minutes at a time as many times as you desired. I had a BLAST, ripping through corners, completing the same race weekend over and over. This game, Rallysport Challenge and GT Legends were the catalyst of my love of cars. Eventually I managed to pick up a physical copy off Ebay to add to my growing collection. This game has lived in my memory like a cattle brand on hide. 
The graphics of this game will not be the best. They aren't the greatest today, but for its time it was great. If you want a nice racing experience that still has a somewhat active community, jump on in. Especially if you have a lightweight machine that can't run intensive stuff like Assetto Corsa. Some of these old racing sims are just fun to get back into!

rFactor, es un simulador de carreras que ha sido una pieza clave en el mundo del automovilismo virtual. Con un enfoque en la simulación realista, ofrece una física de conducción avanzada, un sistema de neumáticos detallado y una jugabilidad altamente personalizable, lo que lo convierte en una opción ideal tanto para entusiastas como para pilotos profesionales.

Uno de los aspectos más destacados de rFactor es su comunidad activa y el soporte para mods, lo que permite agregar una enorme variedad de autos, pistas y mejoras gráficas. Gracias a esto, la experiencia de juego es prácticamente ilimitada, adaptándose a diferentes estilos de conducción y competiciones.

A pesar de ser un título veterano, su jugabilidad sigue siendo sólida. Si buscas un simulador realista con un alto nivel de personalización y una comunidad apasionada, rFactor es una excelente elección para cualquier amante del automovilismo.

With just 2 hours in rFactor, I can already tell why this game still holds up remarkably well, even almost two decades after its release in 2005. It’s a testament to how far ahead of its time it was, especially in terms of physics and driving realism. For any motorsport enthusiast looking for a no-nonsense sim racing experience, rFactor is still worth checking out. That said, it’s also a game that can feel brutal for newcomers because of its learning curve—it’s incredibly hard to master.

The first thing you notice about rFactor is its focus on delivering a pure simulation experience. This isn’t a casual racer where you jump in and start drifting around corners like you’re in an arcade. Instead, it prioritizes realistic physics and detailed handling, which makes every lap on the track a serious challenge. You can feel every mistake you make—pushing too hard into a corner, missing the braking point, or not managing throttle control will send you spinning off the track in no time. The game doesn’t hold your hand, and that’s both a blessing and a curse. For someone looking to improve their driving skills, it’s rewarding. But for a new player, it can feel overwhelming, especially without modern assists that more recent games tend to offer.

Despite its age, the modding community has played a huge role in keeping rFactor alive and relevant. There’s a wealth of user-made tracks, cars, and tweaks available, meaning the game can continue to evolve long after its original release. This level of customization is what has kept it so beloved in the sim racing community. You’re not limited to a set amount of content; you can experiment and expand the game to match your preferences, whether it’s testing new cars or racing on classic tracks from motorsport history. That modding freedom makes rFactor feel timeless in a way that few games from its era can.

The visuals, of course, do show their age—it’s a game from 2005, after all—but if you’re willing to look past that, you’ll find that rFactor still delivers where it counts. The driving experience remains rock-solid, and once you get used to the older presentation, the immersion comes from the sheer challenge of the gameplay. It’s not about flashy graphics or cinematic presentation—it’s about nailing your braking points, understanding car dynamics, and pushing for faster lap times. For a sim, that’s what really matters.

In my 2 hours, I found myself struggling to get to grips with the handling and track layouts, but at the same time, I felt a sense of respect for how well this game still holds up. It demands precision and patience, and mastering it feels like a true accomplishment. It’s easy to see why rFactor is still regarded as a cornerstone of sim racing—it paved the way for so many other sims that came after it, setting a standard for realistic physics that many games continue to chase to this day.

Overall, rFactor is not for the faint of heart. It’s a good game with a steep learning curve that rewards dedication. If you’re willing to put in the time to master its mechanics and explore the modding community, you’ll find a lot of depth and satisfaction here. Even in 2024, it still stands as a solid reminder of what made sim racing special in the first place.

9/10.
